entities.summary:
Air Canada is the flag carrier and largest airline of Canada, founded in 1937 as Trans-Canada Air Lines. Operating from hubs in Toronto Pearson, Montreal Trudeau, and Vancouver, it serves over 50 million passengers annually on routes spanning six continents, with particular strength in transatlantic and transpacific routes.

Air Canada's privatization in 1988 and subsequent 2003 bankruptcy and emergence under restructuring created a leaner carrier that absorbed Canadian Airlines International in 2000, eliminating domestic competition. The SARS outbreak in 2003, 9/11 in 2001, and COVID-19 in 2020 each created severe crises requiring government support and restructuring. Air Canada received C$5.9 billion in COVID aid in 2021.

Air Canada's bilingual operations, serving both English and French Canadian communities as a national requirement, reflect Canada's unique linguistic duality. Its Air Canada Rouge leisure subsidiary and Aeroplan loyalty program (spun off and reacquired) reflect modern airline revenue diversification. The airline's Dreamliner-heavy fleet positioned it for fuel-efficient long-haul expansion. Despite crises, Air Canada maintains Canada's connectivity to global markets and serves as a strategic national infrastructure company.
